To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed an approach to assess the biological activity of chemicals based on the transcription factor activity profile (TF activity profile), which is a quantitative measure of the activity of transcription factor (TF) in a cell.
transcription factor activity profiling reveals signatures of perturbed pathways and cell systems and allows straightforward identification of compounds by their bioactivity.

transcription factor activity profiles are invariant across cell systems, perturbagens, and cell states for perturbations of specific pathways and that the invariant signatures can be used to identify compounds that affect specific pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery, characterization, and application of transcription factor activity profiling (TFAP).
developing and applying a new method for assessing the bioactivity of chemicals.
the identification of the biological activity of chemical compounds and their mode of action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FACTORIAL assay is a powerful tool for identifying the biological activities of compounds, and it is particularly useful for identifying the multiple activities of polypharmacology drugs.
TF activity profiling is a useful tool in assessing the biological activities of chemical compounds.
TF activity profiling allows the identification of compounds that perturb specific biological pathways, and that the TFAPs of these compounds are invariant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transcriptional activity of TFs is a reliable readout of the activity of biological pathways, and TF activity profiling is a useful tool for the assessment of the biological activity of chemicals.
we have established the FACTORIAL as an effective tool for the assessment of the bioactivities of compounds.
TF activity profiling is a powerful method for assessing the bioactivity of a compound by assessing the activity profile of the transcription factors that control gene expression in the target cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activity of a compound can be assessed through its transcription factor activity profile (TF-AP) signature.
one can infer bioactivity of compounds from TFAPs, which can be obtained from cell-based assays.
one can assess the bioactivity of chemicals and drugs by measuring the activities of a small number of transcription factors.
